rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Change only gradient duration to determine whether the tightly clustered early peaks separate with a shallower slope. This also tests whether the marginally resolved later pair benefits from extra gradient time.

Test the highest temperature against injection 1 to probe selectivity within the early three-peak cluster. Higher temperature should also preserve a short last-peak time while revealing whether temperature is a stronger lever than slope.

Keep the favorable high-temperature selectivity and reduce gradient steepness to improve the remaining R = 1.14 pair. The current last peak at 7.03 min leaves room to lengthen the gradient while likely staying below the 10-minute penalty threshold.

The remaining critical pair worsened with a shallower gradient, so test a higher starting organic fraction to alter its selectivity. Keep temperature and duration fixed to assess the window shift while monitoring compression of the early peaks.

Injection 5 reached the maximum CRF; now shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Monitor the two early pairs with the smallest resolution margins, retaining injection 5 as the benchmark.

Narrow the gradient window to give a slope between injections 5 and 6, aiming to restore both early pairs above R = 1.5 while remaining faster than injection 5. The final organic fraction remains comfortably above the estimated last-peak elution composition.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction can improve the limiting pair enough to support a faster fully resolved run. This probes the trade-off between favorable selectivity and compression of the early peaks; injection 7 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Probe temperature selectivity one step below 60 C at the nearly resolved fast method from injection 6. This tests whether a modest temperature change can lift both critical early pairs above 1.5 without lengthening the gradient.

Test the intermediate slope between the fully resolved injection 7 and the slightly under-resolved injection 6. This single-grid refinement seeks a shorter last-peak time while preserving the maximum CRF.

With a maximum-score method secured, test the opposite temperature extreme for a different, potentially better-resolved elution order in the early cluster. The broad, fast gradient should limit late retention while assessing this alternative selectivity regime.

Return to 60 C and flatten the gradient at the higher starting organic fraction to improve the R = 1.28 pair from injection 8. This tests whether that window can provide full resolution with a larger margin for the neighboring pair.

Seek a larger resolution margin around the maximum-score method by modestly reducing its slope. Both critical early pairs improved as the gradient became shallower at this starting composition, and the last peak should remain well below 10 minutes.

Test a shorter programmed gradient with a slope between the fully resolved injections 5 and 7. The endpoint remains above the estimated last-peak elution composition, so all peaks should elute during the gradient while preserving full resolution.

Increase the endpoint one step from injection 14 to test a slightly steeper, faster gradient near the full-resolution boundary. This slope lies between injections 7 and 10, where the limiting pair straddled R = 1.5.

Injection 15 still has a sub-threshold pair despite its rounded CRF of 1.000, so retain injection 7 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method. Test a shallower gradient for a stronger resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Reduce the slope one more step from injection 12 to bring its remaining R = 1.43 pair above threshold. This could establish a second fully resolved starting composition with useful resolution margins and no time penalty.

Compare a lower starting composition at the same slope as injection 7 to isolate its effect on the critical cluster. This fills the untested window between phi0 = 0.05 and 0.15 and checks for an alternative fully resolved operating region.

The nearby faster windows have not improved on injection 7, so test a larger resolution margin at the successful starting composition. Extending injection 16 by two minutes should improve the critical pair while keeping the last peak below the 10-minute penalty threshold.

Return toward the fastest fully resolved region, testing the grid point between injections 7 and 13. This should retain the maximum CRF with slightly more resolution margin than injection 7 and a shorter elution time than injection 13.

Preserve injection 7’s successful gradient slope but end the ramp earlier to test a shorter, lower-organic program. The last peak will likely elute during the hold, so this tests whether full resolution and a last-peak time below 10 minutes can be retained.

Test whether the higher-starting-organic method from injection 17 retains full resolution at a lower temperature. Its R = 1.82 margin for the temperature-sensitive neighboring pair may accommodate this change, providing an alternative maximum-score method at 55 C.

Reduce the endpoint one grid step from injection 22 to improve its two marginal early pairs with a shallower gradient. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially establishing a fully resolved alternative at 55 C.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 23 to lift the remaining R = 1.48 pair above threshold, while raising the endpoint to keep the last peak within the gradient. The estimated last-peak time remains below 10 minutes.
